messages:
maria (support): Hey — customer hitting ImportError after following our quickstart. They ran `poetry install` then `pip install git+https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk.git@main` and `python -c "import redwood"` fails with "ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redwood'". Reported after upgrading to Python 3.10 on mac M1.

emily (support): Oof. Can you paste the minimal repro steps and the stacktrace? Also which package shows up in `pip list`?

maria (support): Repro steps from customer below:
```bash
# cloned inside a fresh dir
poetry new repro-test
cd repro-test
# added dependency in pyproject: redwood-sdk = {git = "https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk.git", rev = "main", extras = ["httpx"]}
poetry install
# then they ran this to make sure latest build is installed
pip install git+https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk.git@main
python -c "import redwood; print(redwood.__version__)"
```
Stacktrace:
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redwood'
```
They also ran `pip show` and saw package name listed as `Name: redwood-sdk` and version `0.9.0.dev0`.

dev-alex: This smells like a packaging metadata mismatch — package name on PyPI vs import name. Historically we published wheel with package name `redwood-sdk` but the importable top-level package is `redwood` (or sometimes `redwood_sdk` if source layout changed). Two quick checks: inside site-packages is there a top-level folder named `redwood` or `redwood_sdk`? Also poetry's extras mapping can be fragile when using git refs.

ops-lee: Also, on mac M1, people sometimes get an older wheel built for x86 in their cache; `pip install` from git should build from sdist though. Another common issue: if the venv was created with `--system-site-packages` there may be an older global `redwood-sdk` shadowing the new install. Ask the customer to run:
```bash
python -c "import sys, site; print(sys.executable); print(site.getsitepackages() if hasattr(site, 'getsitepackages') else site.getusersitepackages()); import pkgutil; print([m.name for m in pkgutil.iter_modules()][:50])"
```

emily (support): Good suggestions. I asked for `ls <venv>/lib/python3.10/site-packages | grep redwood` output; customer sent back: `redwood_sdk-0.9.0.dist-info  redwood_sdk  redwood_sdk-0.9.0-py3.10.egg-info` (no plain `redwood`). So the package is installed under `redwood_sdk` top-level package. That explains the import failure.

maria (support): They said earlier they followed our quickstart which uses `import redwood`. Ooops — looks like the repo layout recently changed the package name to `redwood_sdk` but we didn’t update the docs or wheel top-level package mapping.

dev-alex: Short-term workaround: `python -c "import importlib, sys; sys.path.insert(0, 'path/to/venv/lib/python3.10/site-packages/redwood_sdk'); import redwood as redwood; print('worked')"` — kidding, better: create a tiny shim package by adding a `redwood/__init__.py` that imports from `redwood_sdk` or advise them to run `pip install git+https://...@main#egg=redwood&subdirectory=python` (if packaging supports an egg name mapping) OR simply `pip install redwood-sdk==0.9.0` if that release exposes `redwood` top-level.

ops-lee: For a clean fix ask them to uninstall both artifacts, clear cache, and reinstall pinned release:
```bash
pip uninstall -y redwood redwood-sdk || true
pip cache purge || true
# install a published release that we know exposes 'redwood'
pip install 'redwood-sdk==0.8.7'
python -c "import redwood; print(redwood.__version__)"
```

emily (support): I've escalated to eng with the details and the site-packages snippet. tagging @dev-alex for packaging/CI check. Also added a note to docs team: quickstart must clearly call out the import path for the pinned release.

deploy-bot: New issue created: RDW-SDK-487 - packaging top-level module mismatch (assigned to dev-alex)

maria (support): Customer tried the uninstall + `pip install 'redwood-sdk==0.8.7'` and reports `import redwood` now works. They also said this happened only when mixing `poetry install` + `pip install git+...` — poetry had created an egg-info for `redwood_sdk` from the VCS dependency which then left a different top-level.

dev-alex: Root cause: during a refactor we renamed the Python package directory to `redwood_sdk` but left the published wheel metadata with `packages=find_packages()` so older quickstarts still expect `redwood`. We'll cut a patch to add a compatibility `redwood` package (shim) and update the README and PyPI packaging to expose `redwood` as the package name for imports. Also will add CI check to ensure top-level import path remains stable.

emily (support): Customer ✅. They asked for a recommended long-term command; I gave them `pip install redwood-sdk>=0.9.1` once patch is released. They also want a short note in our quickstart telling folks not to mix poetry VCS extras + pip installs.

maria (support): Closing loop with customer now. Thanks all :thumbsup:
